root_cause.text: The CAN raw socket implementation frees the per-CPU `ro->uniq` storage in `raw_release()` before the deferred RCU callback registered by `can_rx_unregister()` has executed, creating a race window where `raw_rcv()` can access the freed memory within an RCU read-side critical section.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes `free_percpu(ro->uniq)` from `raw_release()` and moves it to a new socket destructor `raw_sock_destruct()` assigned to `sk->sk_destruct`, ensuring that the per-CPU memory is only freed after the RCU callbacks have drained and the socket is destroyed.

bic_trace_step.reason: This commit introduces the vulnerability. It defines 'ro->uniq' as a per-CPU variable, allocates it in raw_init() (lines 312-317), and frees it in raw_release() using free_percpu(ro->uniq) (line 362). However, raw_rcv() can still be executed within an RCU read-side critical section and access 'ro->uniq' (lines 132-138) after raw_release() has freed it, because the unregistration of the receiver (via can_rx_unregister) is deferred and does not guarantee that no more raw_rcv() calls are in progress when free_percpu() is called.
